reasons: Lake identity records case_name_full as Austin v. United States, court as U.S., date_decided as 1993-06-28, and year as 1993.
Lake citations record official cite 509 U.S. 602, parallels 113 S. Ct. 2801 and 125 L. Ed. 2d 488, and vendor-neutral cites 1993 U.S. LEXIS 4407 and 1993 WL 224465.
The opinion states the question as whether the Excessive Fines Clause applies to forfeitures under 21 U.S.C. §§ 881(a)(4) and (a)(7), then says: We hold that it does.
At reporter star 622, the opinion concludes that forfeiture under these provisions constitutes payment to a sovereign as punishment for some offense and is subject to the Excessive Fines Clause.
The proposition does not overclaim an excessiveness standard; the opinion expressly remanded that question.
The opinion is directly about in rem civil forfeiture under 21 U.S.C. §§ 881(a)(4) and (a)(7).
The holding makes Austin central to whether the Excessive Fines Clause applies to civil forfeiture, supporting the Civil Asset Forfeiture home role.
residual_risks: Anchor is an editorial corpus role; no separate Civil Asset Forfeiture home-page definition was disclosed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If desired, describe the role as anchor for Excessive Fines Clause applicability to civil forfeiture.
